items.stem: A firm wants confidential documents to stay protected even after they leave the tenant by email. What should be applied?

options.text: A sensitivity label that applies encryption and usage rights
options.rationale: Correct: label-based encryption travels with the content.

options.text: A label with no protection settings
options.rationale: A label without protection does not enforce anything.
Network rules do not protect portable documents.
Deletion is not protection of shared content.

items.explanation: Correct: label-based encryption travels with the content.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when rolling out a new DLP policy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Start in simulation/test mode and review matches before enforcing
options.rationale: Correct: simulation reduces disruptive false positives.

options.text: Tune sensitive information types to the organisation's real identifiers
Begin in hard-block mode for all users immediately
Apply no conditions so everything is blocked

items.explanation: Correct: simulation reduces disruptive false positives.

items.stem: A compliance team must find who accessed a client's files during a dispute. Which Purview capability answers this?

options.rationale: Correct: audit logs record access activity for investigation.
Labels show protection, not who accessed files.
DLP prevents loss; it is not an access-history search.
